AnsibleForms installer.
It installs, upgrades and maintains AnsibleForms.

usage.upgrade: upgrade to a newer version, showing its release notes first

--yes answers the remaining questions with their defaults.

install.roleHelp:
This installs AnsibleForms {version}.
A controller is the complete application.
A Runner only runs playbooks for a controller.
install.roleControllerHint:
The web interface, its database and its own Runner.
On this server or on Kubernetes.
Choose this for a first installation.
install.roleRunnerHint:
It runs the playbooks of an AnsibleForms installed elsewhere.
For example in another network, a DMZ or another datacenter.
It talks to AnsibleForms over a single WebSocket.
install.modeKubernetesHint:
The Helm chart, on the cluster that kubectl reaches.
It is served behind an ingress.
install.runtimeHelp:
Docker and Podman are both installed on this server.
Choose the one that runs AnsibleForms.
runtime.dockerHint:
Docker Engine with its compose plugin.
The containers restart together with Docker.
runtime.podmanHint:
Podman, rootless or as root.
A systemd unit starts the containers at boot.
runtime.dockerInstallHint:
Installed with Docker's official script (get.docker.com).
The compose plugin is included.
runtime.podmanInstallHint:
Installed from this distribution's packages.
podman-compose is included.
install.dirHelp:
The compose file and its .env with the secrets are stored here.
So is all the data: database, forms, playbooks and logs.
install.nameHelp:
Its containers are named after it: af_app, af_db, af_rte.
Different names let several instances share one server.
install.portHelp: The port the web interface listens on.
runner.portHelp:
Outbound, only the health checks listen on this port.
They are reachable from this server only.
Inbound, AnsibleForms connects to the Runner on this port.
runner.addressHelp:
The address AnsibleForms uses to reach this server.
An inbound Runner receives the connection from AnsibleForms.
install.tlsHelp:
How browsers connect to it.
HTTPS is strongly recommended: logins and secrets go through it.
install.tlsSelfHint:
A certificate created here for this server's names.
It is valid for ten years.
Browsers ask you to accept it once.
install.tlsOwnHint:
Your own certificate and key, in PEM format.
From your CA, or from Let's Encrypt.
install.tlsOffHint:
Plain HTTP on the port.
For a reverse proxy in front that handles HTTPS.
For example nginx, Traefik or a load balancer.
install.adminPasswordHelp:
The password of the admin user, the first account.
Leave it empty to generate a strong one.
It is shown at the end.
review.name: Name
runner.appUrlHelp:
The address of the AnsibleForms this Runner works for.
The same address people open in a browser.
runner.modeHelp:
Both modes use a single WebSocket.
Only the side that opens the connection differs.
runner.modeOutboundHint:
The Runner opens the connection to AnsibleForms and keeps it open.
Only traffic from this server to AnsibleForms, on its port.
Nothing from outside reaches this server.
For a DMZ, NAT, or a zone that allows no incoming connections.
runner.modeInboundHint:
AnsibleForms opens the connection to the Runner.
It connects to this server's address and port.
For networks where the central side opens every connection.

The Helm chart's runner mode, on the cluster that kubectl reaches.

Different names let several instances share one server.
install.dirHelpNative:
AnsibleForms, Node.js, Python and the settings go here.
So does all the data: forms, playbooks and logs.
The database itself is kept by MariaDB.

Take it over to upgrade it from here.

detect.foundHelpCurrent:
Take it over to manage it from here: its backups, status and next upgrades.
A second installation beside it could clash on ports, the database or folders.
detect.foundHelpNone:

A second installation beside it could clash on ports, the database or folders.
detect.choose: What do you want to do?
detect.adoptHint:
The installer remembers where it is and how it runs, then upgrades it.
It backs up the database first and can roll back.
detect.adoptCurrentHint:
The installer remembers where it is and how it runs.
Nothing is changed now.
detect.alongside: Install a new AnsibleForms beside it anyway
detect.alongsideHint:
A separate installation, with its own folder, ports and database.
The one found is left as it is.
detect.alongsideHelp:
A second AnsibleForms needs its own ports, folder and database.
The installer refuses a folder or container names in use, but it cannot check everything.
detect.alongsideConfirm: Install a second AnsibleForms on this server?
detect.unattended:
AnsibleForms is already installed on this server and the installer does not manage it.
Run the installer without --yes to choose what to do.
When only one is found, ansibleforms-installer upgrade --yes takes it over and upgrades it.
detect.cannotAdopt: AnsibleForms was found on this server, but the installer cannot upgrade it: see why above.
detect.adoptReview: The installer will remember this installation in {file}:
detect.adoptCompose:
The upgrade backs up the database, docker-compose.yml and .env first.
It then replaces docker-compose.yml with the one of the ansibleforms/docker repository.
The .env keeps every value; the keys the new version needs are added. The data folder is kept.
detect.adoptRunner:
The upgrade rewrites docker-compose.yml for the new RTE image.
The .env and the data folder are kept as they are.
detect.adoptDatabaseRunner:
This Runner runs in database mode, deprecated since 7.3: its RTE holds the database settings of AnsibleForms.
The upgrade moves it to the installer's Runner layout, outbound or inbound, under the same runner.
Its old files are backed up, and the old container is removed only once the new one is connected.
detect.adoptKube:
The release's current values are saved next to installer.json.
The upgrades apply them again, with the chart of the new version.
detect.adoptNative:
The upgrade puts the new release in releases/ and moves the current link.
The settings and the data folder are kept as they are.
detect.adopted: The installer now manages this installation ({file}).
detect.unmanagedTitle: On this server, not managed by the installer:
detect.statusAdopt: Run ansibleforms-installer upgrade to take it over and upgrade it.
detect.why_notCompose:
Its containers were not started with Docker Compose.
Upgrade them by hand, the way they were started.
detect.why_noComposeFile:
The installer may not read {file} in {dir}.
Run the installer as root or as the folder's owner.
detect.why_noComposeFileRoot:
The installer cannot read {file} in {dir}, even as root.
Check the file's permissions and its SELinux label, then run the installer again.
detect.why_missingComposeFile:
There is no {file} in {dir}, the folder its containers were started from.
Put it back, or start the containers again from the folder that has it, then run the installer again.
detect.why_notRepoLayout:
Its compose file does not follow the ansibleforms/docker repository.
That is the services mysqldb, app and rte, in containers <name>_db, _app and _rte.
Upgrade it by hand: change the image tags in its compose file, then run compose up -d.
detect.why_externalDb:
Its database is outside its compose project.
The installer only backs up the project's own database: upgrade it by hand.
detect.why_runnerLayout:
This Runner was not set up by the installer.
Upgrade it by hand, or install a new Runner with the installer and approve it in AnsibleForms.
detect.why_nativeLayout:
Its folder is not the installer's layout (releases/, current, app.env and rte.env).
Upgrade it by hand, the way it was installed.
detect.why_noHelm:
It runs on Kubernetes, but not as a release of the ansibleforms Helm chart (or helm is missing here).
Upgrade it with the tool that deployed it.
detect.why_argoCD:
It runs on Kubernetes, managed by the Argo CD Application {app}.
The installer leaves it alone: upgrade it in Argo CD, by changing the chart version of the Application.
detect.why_unknownVersion:
Its version could not be read.
Start it so it answers on its port, then run the installer again.
detect.why_unmanaged:
AnsibleForms {version} answers on port {port}, but no engine manages it (run from source or by hand).
The installer cannot upgrade it. A new installation could clash with its ports or its database.
detect.why_unmanagedRunner:
An AnsibleForms RTE answers on port {port}, but no engine manages it (run from source or by hand).
The installer cannot upgrade it. A new installation could clash with its port.
detect.short_notRepoLayout: its compose file is not the ansibleforms/docker one
detect.short_externalDb: its database is outside its compose project
detect.short_runnerLayout: this Runner was not set up by the installer
detect.short_nativeLayout: its folder is not in the installer's layout
detect.short_noHelm: not a release of the ansibleforms Helm chart
migrate.gone:
The RTE container of the Runner in {dir} is gone, so its runner's name and token cannot be read.
Start it again, or install a new Runner and approve it in AnsibleForms.
migrate.intro:
This Runner runs in database mode (7.2): its RTE holds the database settings of AnsibleForms.
The upgrade moves it to a socket mode and drops those settings. It stays the runner {name}: the new RTE signs in with the runner's token, and AnsibleForms moves the runner itself, without an approval.
migrate.nameHelp:
The name of its runner under Connections > Runners, the one this RTE registered itself as.
The new RTE signs in under this name (RTE_NAME).
migrate.nameHelpGuessed:
This RTE did not register itself (RTE_REGISTER=0): an admin added its runner by hand.
Type the name its runner has under Connections > Runners. The new RTE signs in under it (RTE_NAME).
migrate.name: Runner name
migrate.needName:
This RTE did not register itself (RTE_REGISTER=0), so its runner's name is not known.
Run the installer without --yes to type it.
migrate.tokenMissing:
The installer cannot read a token from this RTE (RTE_TOKEN).
The runner's token is the password of its credential in AnsibleForms, under Connections > Credentials: with it the runner keeps its name and its jobs.
Without it, a join token adds a new runner, and the old one is retired by hand.
migrate.tokenChoice: How should the new RTE sign in?
migrate.tokenTypeHint:
The password of the runner's credential in AnsibleForms.
The runner keeps its name, its jobs and the forms that name it.
migrate.tokenJoin: Join as a new runner with a join token
migrate.tokenJoinHint:
A join token of Connections > Runners adds a new runner at once.
Retire the old runner afterwards.
migrate.joinNameHelp: A join token cannot give the runner {old} a new token, so the new RTE joins under another name.
migrate.needToken:
The installer cannot read a token from this RTE (RTE_TOKEN).
Run the installer without --yes to type the runner's token, or give a join token with --join.
migrate.portHelp:
AnsibleForms connects to the new RTE on this port, served over HTTPS with a pinned certificate.
A port the old RTE holds is freed first, so the Runner is offline until the new one connects.
migrate.tokenJoinShort: a join token: a new runner
migrate.oldRemoved: {containers}, removed once the new RTE is connected
migrate.reviewHelp:
The upgrade backs up the compose file and .env to {dir}.
It writes the installer's Runner layout without the database settings (DB_*) and starts the new RTE beside the old one.
Once the new RTE is connected to AnsibleForms, the old container is stopped and removed. If it does not connect, you can roll back.
migrate.confirm: Move this Runner to {mode} mode with AnsibleForms {to}?
migrate.backedUp: Backed up the old files to {dir}
migrate.stoppingFirst: Stopping the old RTE first: it holds port {port}
migrate.waiting: Waiting for the new RTE to connect to AnsibleForms at {url}
migrate.connected: The new RTE is connected as runner {name} ({mode})
migrate.removingOld: Stopping and removing the old RTE: {containers}
migrate.removeFailed:
The old RTE could not be removed: {error}
Remove it by hand: the new one already runs the jobs.
migrate.pending:
AnsibleForms knows no runner by that name, so the new RTE asked to join and waits for an approval.
Reject that request under Connections > Runners, then run the upgrade again with the runner's name. Log: {container}
migrate.exited:
The new RTE stopped.
Check its log: {runtime} logs {container}
migrate.notConnected:
The new RTE did not connect to AnsibleForms in time.
Check its log: {runtime} logs {container}
migrate.noRollback:
The new RTE is connected and AnsibleForms has moved runner {name}, so the installer does not go back.
The old files are in installer-backups.
migrate.rollback:
Put the database-mode Runner back?
The old files come back and the old container starts again.
migrate.rolledBackNote: If AnsibleForms already moved runner {name} to {mode}, set its mode back to database under Connections > Runners.
migrate.done: The Runner (AnsibleForms {version}) runs in socket mode
migrate.doneKept:
AnsibleForms moved runner {name} to the new mode itself: no approval is needed.
Its jobs and the forms that name it are unchanged.
migrate.doneJoined:
Runner {name} joined with the join token.
Retire the old runner {old} under Connections > Runners, and point the forms that name it at {name}.
kube.adoptValues: Saving the current values of {release} to {file}
compose.envAdded:
The new version's .env adds: {keys}.
The existing values are kept, new secrets are generated, and the old .env is saved next to it.
compose.envBlocked:
The .env lacks database settings the new version needs: {keys}.
They cannot be made up for an existing database. Add them by hand (see the Database section of the ansibleforms/docker README), then upgrade again. Nothing was changed.
compose.seedReplaced:
data/seed.yaml is replaced by the new version's: the app now dials its local RTE (inbound) with a credential.
The old seed is saved next to it.
compose.seedCustom:
data/seed.yaml was changed by hand, so it is kept. The new version's is saved as {file}.
Merge it (the local RTE now needs rte_mode: inbound and a credential), or playbooks may not run.
compose.seedWriting: Replacing data/seed.yaml with the new version's
